Story mode · Kokoro podcast mock

A story that travels: studio, classroom, café, code

Two hosts explain one real change, and the story moves as it unfolds: a server room while it is broken, a classroom or lecture hall to teach it, a coffee house to argue the options, a train or a street for what happened over time, the matrix for the code, a rooftop at dawn to wrap up. Each chapter has a mood, and the setting follows it: rain and red light while it is broken, a light bulb when it clicks, sunrise when it is solved. Ask a follow-up and it is added to the story as new chapters. Every line is Kokoro-82M audio, embedded in this page; the follow-up answers are prepared here, and in the app the story writer would write them.

    Maya af_heart · Jonah am_michael · Kokoro on this node
    Mock: answers are prepared for the suggested questions. In the app the story writer reads the change history and the story so far, writes new chapters as data (a location, a mood, a visual and lines), and Kokoro speaks them on this node.

    Story mode

    Settings → Story mode, on this node. The instructions steer every story and every follow-up answer. Narration runs here with Kokoro, so no API key is needed.

    Format
    Sent to the story writer with every request. Empty uses the built-in podcast instructions.
    Locations and mood
    The writer picks a location and a mood for every chapter. A location you turn off is replaced by the podcast studio.
    Code
    These apply the next time a story opens; try them here, then reopen an episode. Size and max lines go to the writer.
    Narration · Kokoro
    onnx-community/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX · q8 · CPU · Apache-2.0 · downloads once, on first use
    Lines are cached per story and voice, so replays cost nothing. This Mac took about 3 seconds per line on CPU, so a story or a follow-up answer starts after a short wait.
    Changing a voice re-generates that episode on this node. Test voices plays the sample clips made with af_heart and am_michael.
